Updated Review
*********************
Undoubtedly DTG have improved the EA version of this sim in a number of ground-breaking and interesting ways; Rain droplets, snow effects, smashed windscreens and weather...all looking pretty good.
However there are some extremely worrying issues like;
- the extreme lack of attention to detail on the base game + updates and DLC’s.
- The complete lack of presence of jet engines...Still.
- the complete disregard of the communities concerns and requests...more interested in poor quality DLC's.
I had extremely high hopes for DTG and FSW and I gave it every opportunity...I can only apologise to each and every person who bought FSW on my recommendation.  I had literally no idea that DTG would behave the way they have, although I realise now I should have known it right from the start!
At one point I was involved with DTG, I offered my time to review and provide feedback on Beta testing.  I was speaking to the team directly and the impression of that team was not a good one, the hope and promise I felt was possible for FSW was totally destroyed when I spoke to the team directly and realised their true priorities were not aligned with the community properly.
FIRST Look Review
*************************
Peoples initial Impressions of this EA title are mixed with raw emotions surrounding the highly anticipated rebirth of FSX.  If Dovetail fail to meet expectations (which are very high) the catastrophic backlash could be significant.
This is currently in EA, and there are bugs and crashes.  The number of aircraft is limited and there are no jets whatsoever.  Controller configurations do not appear to be retained and there are some odd sensitivity issues surrounding controllers but no Calibration tool to help resolve (there is a solution).
All that aside, if you can see past that, actually DTG have made a pretty good job of this title...IF EA means that there is much work to do!
Positives & Negatives
================
The menu system is updated but familiar to the FSX faithful.
The flight model seems much better and it comes with A2A's AccuSim as standard!  Plus DTG have associations with some really big hitters from the FSX 3rd party pool, not to mention confirmed + Licensed access to the Airbus A320.
The Flight planner has had a significantly improved update...BUT ATM it is limited to being useful for only VFR and not yet suitable for IFR.
Graphically there have been improvements; FPS is a fairly stable 30 or more if you wish to sacrifice certain enhancements.  Push it too far though and FPS will take a massive hit and possibly crash the game.
Native support for TrackIR - Works brilliant, no issues whatsoever.
Native support for multiple screens - Don't use unless you have a trio of GTX 1080's onboard.  It will not look pretty, and will likely crash.
Handful of airplanes beautifully created by DTG and Carenado...I don't think any of them are finalised inside?  At least I hope not.  They do have advanced physics applied and also some very nice looking additional animated modelling.
Rain....If you don't know about this you should.  Just fantastic!
Missions are probably my favourite thing about FSX, now we have a tool to help us create our own and share on the Steam workshop!  Brilliant!
The tutorials are very similar to FSX but definitely updated and improved.  A little more work here and I think this will be a real positive selling point for FSW.
Overall I am more than happy and to be honest a little excited.  As always this is EA.....Don;t buy expecting bells and whistles, but definitely a potential competitor for X-Plane 11 (Despite what others might tell you!).

In my opinion FSW, once out of early access, will be a good option for non-hardcore simmers because it's easy to use and it includes all the essentials to start enjoying flying simulation (Accu-sim flight model, Orbx FTX Global scenery, good quality planes, native multiplayer and now TrueSKY weather and clouds).
I think Flight Sim World will attract new people into the flight sim community just like FSX:SE did before.
Note that being early access, it still has issues: low frame-rates due to lack of optimisation, a few bugs here and there, the choice of aircraft is limited for now, with just 7 GA planes.
So my advice is: if you don't like dealing with early access products wait some time before buying (but you will likely pay a bit more), otherwise you can get it now and, if you want, provide feedback to DTG.
Of course FSW is not going to be comparable with products like X-Plane or P3D which are designed, respectively, for the enthusiast and professional market, but it will be a good choice for beginners and casual players. Not everyone has the money to buy professional level software or the spare time to learn 3rd party software like Ortho4XP.
Finally, some people say that FSW looks exactly like (or even worse than) FSX. It's an argument that doesn't stand since FSW includes Orbx FTX global, which would cost you more than the game itself if you had to buy it as an add-on for FSX. And TreSKY looks great even in comparison to expensive weat add-ons such as ASCA or XEnviro. I suspect those people were using FSX with a bunch of add-ons and don't even remember how it originally looked with default scenery.

I have been a MSFSer since version 4.0. starting in 1994. I have enjoyed FSX since 2007 and have logged over 11,000 hrs on just the steam version alone. I must say FSW is NOT a step forward but a step BACKWARD in terms of the experience. There is NO WOW!!! There is only FRUSTRATION and DISAPPOINTMENT.
You would think with a new sim purchased from Microsoft that Dovetail would present what already was and ADD to it. Instead we have stepped backwards. Just a typical example. We have known that the ATC voices in FSX was inadequate. We have had Editvoicepak (and others I suppose) to improve this. FSW's ATC voices are worse than FSX. They are too slow and mechanical. I expected something more human like and fluid. I expected a little bit of static on the radios. I expected accents according to regions. This would have WOWED me. But as I said it is worse than FSX. Very mechanical and muffled and don't even talk about the ATC UI.
Another example is airport quality. We have become used to developers like FSDreamteam, FlyTampa, Taxi2Gate and ORBX giving us some deep, rich realistic runway textures and as real as life buildings and building textures to simulate the real world to 99% of reality. FSW takes us back to FS98 standards of airport scenery quality.
Here are the major frustrations
I cannot seem to see any way to download realworld weather. All you have is presets. This is a step backward.
Your flight planning map is a joke. No airways. No intersections. Another backward step. I'd better see your flight planning map have the ability to have airways, SIDS/STARS and teh ability to update AIRAC cycles.
You cannot pause the sim without getting an overlay over your screen. This is frustrating when you want to pause to zoom in on the instrument panel. What's the point of doing this????
I set the weather to stormy. Obviously solid IFR and requested a VFR clearance and got one with no questions asked. FSX would have denied me. HOW IS THIS AN UPGRADE???
PUT BACK THE MENU ITEMS ON TOP.
All we have is 2 menu items - Options and views. Views gives us the normal FSX options but Options only has pause, simulation rate and sound on/off. How the hell is that an improvement????
Aircraft.
What the hell? We had piston, turbo prop, jetliner and helicopter aircraft models. FSW only gives us piston powered airplanes. HOW THE HELL IS THIS AN IMPROVEMENT????
FREE FLIGHT
If it's called free flight, why the hell do I have to make a flight plan that appears on the GPS???
INSTRUMENTS
You cannot change the altiude on the G1000 in the seneca nor on the stec of the Mirage. The left gyro compass in the Mirage does not work.
LIGHTS
No strobe lights. Nav lights do not work (at least during the day)
I'm getting tired of listing faults.
POSITIVES
I love the AI traffic. You get traffic registered based on countries. You won't get a Mexican airplane flying in Dubai.
I like that you get an actual rotating reflector cup in the rotating beacon. This has never been simulated before.
Cockpit shadows are amazing.
Yes you do get raindrops on the windscreen and side glass.
Saw some vibrating instruments in an airplane. Not all aircraft have it and not all instruments vibrate.
Yes we now run on 64 bit. However with just the stock sim running at max and some really nasty weather loaded I was eating up over 3MB of memory.
I like the fact that you have to log solo time before you do the checkride.
I will be sticking to FSX and if you are curious I'd say DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY

This title is one that I was interested in from the moment I came across it prior to its actual release. As an avid fan of platformers and games where you have a certain degree of creative control (level editors), this game fit me like a glove. And once I saw that the game was going to recieve the online treatment, I knew I needed it
.
I have no regrets.
On its surface, the gameplay is your average platformer. You can move with WASD, jump with the spacebar, and interact with certain elements of the world with your mouse. There is a wall jump mechanic, and you can even single wall jump. The best part: it all feels very fluid and responsive. But once you add in the multiplayer race aspect and the level customization, the game becomes much,
more complicated. You want to make it possible, but you also want to make it very difficult so that you and only you can finish. You also want to figure out the fastest way to complete the level (which is set up differently every time you play) so that you have higher chances of winning.
There is a very good variety of level gimmicks available to you, but most of them need to be unlocked. That's not necessarily a bad thing though: the two stages that are available to you from the get-go, while fairly basic, are good for honing your skills in the game in a relatively safe environment. My personal favorite stage is unfortunately the one that you unlock last, but I can't really fault the developers for putting it there because the gimmick is fairly eye-straining.
For all you fans of hats out there (and I know you are out there), the game offers a decent selection of characters and character specific cosmetic items for use in game. All characters are balanced equally, so no one will get an advantage if they choose to use one character over another. The current build of the online beta as of the time of me writing this review has some issues with cosmetics, so I would recommend local play if you can swing it if you want to use them.
Finally, the current online beta runs exceptionally well for being a beta. There are public games available for anyone at most times of the day, and hosting a public game is as simple as specifying a region and pressing a button. If you don't have people to play with locally, you can probably find someone online to play with. Be warned: there is no chat right now, but one might be planned for the future. If you feel the need for a chat, I would recommend waiting for a bit before purchasing. Last I checked there is an emote system coming soon, but even then I'm aware that doesn't work for everyone.

You're given a house to explore at your leisure.  It's filled with hundreds of items for you to pick up and drop on the floor.  All around the house you discover lights to leave on, faucets to run and toilets to flush.  The most important items are the notes because they are the vehicle for character development.  Some also prompt voice-overs.
The player is an observer, not a participant.  Therefore, don't expect a sense of progression beyond simply learning about the characters.  The moment you exist in the world is a snapshot of times gone by.
The environment is immersive and the voice acting is phenomenal.  These two things ensure that Gone Home carries emotional impact.  I definitely don't feel like my time was wasted here.  But at the same time I just don't see enough reason to recommend it.

The Crew is not a good game.
While the concept of the game sounds great, Ivory Tower fails to execute it well. The cars all feel similar (the performance cars all feel the same as each other, the raid cars feel the same, etc) and don't control as good compared to other driving games. The game borrows many ideas from previous Ubisoft releases that don't really translate that well in a car. The online community for this game may as well not be there. There is a chat in-game but in the 20+ hours I've put into this game I've yet to see one person use it.. which can make it hard for people to find a Crew to party with in-game. Invites to races and events other people usually go unaccepted. While a large portion of the Crew relies on having a Crew, the game doesn't have a whole lot to offer for people looking for a single player experience.
The map for this game is huge and allows you to drive from the east coast of the United States to the west coast. In between are rocky mountains, open plains, wildlife darting across the road, cops, pedestrian vehicles getting in the way, little towns at the end of dirt roads and huge cities. In between all these are hundreds and hundreds (it seems like) of events. There's a handful of events such as staying in between the lines, smashing through 'gates', going as fast as you can, mountain climbing, and more. Completing these events (and other races) reward you with a score based on how well you did and are rewarded with different car parts than you can equip to cars; increasing their overall stats. Instead of climbing towers to unlock portions of the map; making you work a little for your progress, the Crew has you drive up to the satellite dishes located by a blinking aura on your map and GPS.
The story is extremely dull, laughable and perdictable.You play as Alex, a man wrongly jailed for the death of his friend. You have the chance you redeem your freedom as FBI Agent Zoe sends you information on the man who killed your friend, and she believes the police officer, Coburn, who arrested you is working behind the scenes with Shiv. You must race your way to the top, earn your ink, and take down Shiv. The music is subpar, instantly forgettable and I found a hard time finding something I enjoyed listening to in-game.
If you're interested in the Crew to get your racing game fix I would suggest looking elsewhere. There's plenty of other racing games out there that are multiple times better that'd you actually enjoy. Also, uPlay sucks.

TLDR: Quality tile based movement dungeon crawler in the vein of the classic Dungeon Master. Focus heavily on puzzles solving, finding secret passage and real time combat. You might not lke it if you are looking for an elaborate story or rich character development. Recommended.
This is a true inheritor of the classic Dungeon Master. The game probablyoffers  the widest range of puzzles, and traps in the genre, they will challenge your mind and sometimes your dexterity as well.
The other charateristic feature, is 3D tiled real time combat. Although you move in "step, tile by tile, and you only have a 90°-120° view, this is a real 3D engine. monsters don't stop while you think or search your inventory, it's all in real time, and you'd better make quick decisions. Monsters behaviors are more elaborate than usual, and even late in the game combats are challenging, and you'll never feel OP.
On the other hand character development is pretty basic, you'll be around level 15 by game's end and you merely assign 1 skill point each level. You manage a party of 4 adventurers, but options are nothing close to Baldur or Wizardry.
There is a plot, your group ran ageound on a lost island and looks for a way to escape. But the game is not about storytelling or fulilling side quests or anything like that. Just about progressing on the main line, although the levels are accesible in various order.
The game is not exactly hardcore, but still on many occasion it is rather hard.
Production is good, and in this speicifc genre this is a very good game.

From the outside, VVVVVV may just look like another retro-styled game that uses its retro factor to hide the fact that it's just another generic platformer. While the former may be true, this is definitely not your average platformer.
The story of this game is simple: you're a captain of a spaceship and your crew has been scattered through another dimension due to some interference. You need to find them and stop the interference. The graphic style is heavily inspired by the Commodore 64's graphics, while the sountrack is more reminiscent of that of the NES. Both of these work great together, although they might not be amusing for someone is tired of retro styled indie games.
VVVVVV is a metroidvania game: meaning that you can explore the dimension you're in looking for all sorts of things (crew members, trinkets, teleporters). What makes VVVVVV so special however is that you can't jump, but you can flip gravity so that you'll go up instead of down, and vice-versa. The concept is easy to learn (but incredibly hard to master), and leads to many creative levels. There will be some levels
that will usually frustrate the crap out of you, but at the same time you'll have a blast trying to figure out how to get through them (unless you are
easily frustrated, in which case, you should stay away from this game). On top of the main game, there are tons of other features that will keep you playing for hours, such as collecting all of the trinkets, time trials, various game modes (
where the entire game is flipped upside down and
where if you die once you have to restart the game), and even a level creator.
VVVVVV will make you want to break your keyboard and you will love every minute of it. What makes this game even better is that it's often on sale for a low price (sometimes even $0.49!). This is a must have for those looking for a challenge.

SUMMARY:
Cook, Serve, Delicious! is a new style of cooking management game. It follows the typical format for restaurant games of upgrading equipment and buying new menu items, and customers ordering, you preparing the food while they impatiently wait, and serving them for a rating. But CSD takes it to the next level – it is a well-designed simulator that may seem like a casual game on first glance, but it is fast paced and requires precision to be successful.
CSD allows you the option of playing with a keyboard, a controller, or a mouse, but the game seems to be designed more with a keyboard usage in mind. The food items come with preset combinations of hotkeys to press, so it’s much quicker and easier to remember the combinations in order. The keyboard controls help make this game more immersive.
POSITIVES:
-High replayability value.
-Nice graphics. Clear, bright, and gorgeously made.
-Fast pace and stress level makes me feel like I’m really back working in a restaurant.
-Mini games make CSD more interesting, such as Iron Chef challenges in Career Mode and a betting system.
-Hilarious in-game e-mails.
-Streamlined and easy to use UI.
-Player can switch out the menu items from day to day, making it a bit more challenging and interesting.
-With the “Battle Kitchen” expansion, there are five different challenge modes to further test your skills separate from the campaign mode, including an endurance mode and a weekly challenge with leaderboards.
NEGATIVES:
-There is no option to scrap the dish or start over if you make a mistake, so accuracy and precision matter.
-Gets repetitive very quickly. It’s best to play this game in short spurts rather than long binge sessions.
-Little restaurant customization.
-High frequency of cleaning tasks (flushing the toilet, setting rat traps, etc.) in addition to cooking. These are pretty time consuming, but can be reduced later with upgrades.
9/10. Challenging, fun, and addictive.

Being a flight simmer from 2013, I have mixed feeling about FSW. Dovetail Games clearly tries to reproduce a different flight simulator from FSX:SE, but it is some kind of "remake" of FSX, with GA aircrafts designed by themselves. I still find lots of problems from FSX that hasn't been solved, such as the performance problems that exists (No optimization to multi-core processors, I mean we are in 2017 right?), or the awful low frame rate even in low settings for my specs. (only 30fps, whereas I achieve this in FSX on high settings with AS A320, AS EGLL, GSX, REX4, HD textures of the airport @3840*2160 fullscreen). So I will not recommend FSW right now as it is still on very Early Access (still lots of room for improvement until the final release, check KSP).
i7-6700k
16Gb RAM
GTX 1070
Postive stuffs:
-Good looking rain droplets on the windshield (
)
-Nice work on the existent airplanes (lots of buttons are working, even the fuses, great look and texture of the aircrafts)
-Nice UI display of the main menu with the music
-Good idea to teach the basics for the new simmers with the trainings, missions and scenarios
-Nice shadow and reflection effects in the cockpit during the day
-Cheaper than P3D and X-Plane 11
Negative stuffs:
-Bad performance (As said above)
-No jet aircrafts (I know it is Early Access, I'm not expecting a B737 but maybe doing a Cirrus SF50 or Citation Mustang?)
-Really bad flying conditions at night, you can't see anything outside the cockpit (
)
-Outdated terrain and buildings (Dating from before 2008, proof: no terminal 3 in PEK/ZBAA)
-No visible or obvious warning of stall, overspeed or too low (It was good in FSX in my opinion, but it might be justified)
-Physics not realistic enough (Opening a door in flight should at least cause something different in flight handling compared to when it is fully closed)
-Snow effects and rain effects outside the cockpit are still the same to FSX
Things that are awaited:
-
, available on Steam AND/OR SimMarket or any 3rd party market (build one yourself if you want) if possible
-Optimization of multi-core processors, improving performance
-Add waypoints on the map, not just VORs and NDBs
-Checklists, as mentioned during your Twitch live on May 11th,2017
In overall, there is still room for improvement but I refunded FSW and not recommend for now. Will buy again and modify this review when there will be a huge update that is worth it.

I think that a lot of people, here, are comparing this sim with the most recent, FINISHED games, with gaming grapphics, but this is not the case. We're talking about a flight simulator, which asks a lot more from the computer and is still a compromise between graphics and the flight model. Let's not forget, this is not a game, but a simulator and a flight simulator is meant to provide a realistic flying experience and cool graphics are a nice bonus. Non the less, we want emersion and even with the fact that the graphics need a lot of work, I see a lot of potential. The aircraft graphics look great. I think the reflection in the water is very well on it's way (some bathymetry would be nice). Also rain effects and fog are very realistic, even much more then what I'm used to from P3D.  The lighter colored textures are not very nice, they're way too bright. On the other hand, the darker land and vegitation textures give a reasonable idea of what the sim is aiming for and what I see is pretty close to FTX Global in my P3D.  The roads are an outright disaster. I never use roads, because I think they look much too fake, but the roads in FSW are the worst I've seen sa far. This need a dramatic upgrade, or a function to remove them. When flying I was pleasently surprised, I think the feeling of flying is actually very nice. The glide slopes, on the other hand, need adjustment, they totaly threw me off and I had a hard time landing, becasue it feels like I'm so much lower to the ground then I normally am. Also brakes of several aircraft need work. The emersion of the cockpit is actually very nice, every button I tried so far, was usable and the movement of everything that can move looks great. Also the gauges seem to work very nicely and the vibration of the airframe gave me a very realistic feel.
I hear a lot of people complain about framerates, but again, this is a flight simulator, there's a lot more going on than we know from any game there is. A flight simulator asks a whole lot more power of the pc and you need a beast of pc to really be able to turn up the settings. I think that a lot of people are pushing the setting beyond what their computer is capable of, resulting in low FPS and a stuttering sim. I've turned up every setting as high as possible and I'm running a pretty steady 30FPS, in heavy weather, on a big airport and the sim is smooth as butter! Much smoother than I know from FSX and P3D.
For controller setup, I really hope tehre will be something simillar to FSUIPC, I never been a real fan of the FSX style controller setup. I like a litle more depth.
This sim is far from finished, a lot has to be done, but let's not forget, that's what early access is for, getting feedback from the users to bring the endresult to a satisfying level. What I see here is a whole lot of potential! If you expect a finished product, then dont get this sim, there's a lot of work to be done, but if you can handle a sim that is still under construction and you like to have a voice in working towards the endresult, I think this sim is very flyable and a good start for a very promissing future.

Gone Home is an atmospheric first person exploration game which takes place in the mid-1990s. You play as Katie, a young woman who has finally come home after a year abroad.
When you, Katie, return home, you find that the house is completely empty and your family is missing. The only clue that you have to-go by is a note left on the front door by your younger sister Sam.
The whole game is you exploring your home to find out what happened to your family while you were away and what has happened in the past few weeks
You can pick up everything and explore every corner of the house, and along the way you will find clues and secrets which will trigger messages left by your sister. These little messages, as well as the lore you find around the house, will help you discover what is going on.
The game has several core themes such as family, depression, and sexuality
One of the things I loved about this game is how rich it is in terms of nostalgia, and not just for those who grew up in the 90s.
Sure Gone Home is filled with wonderful memories from the 90s such as old consoles, cassettes and VHS tapes but the game promotes the idea of childhood nostalgia as a whole as opposed to just one era.
Finding condoms in your parent’s bedroom, looking through your siblings stuff, keeping old board games that none of you have played in years… these are all little snippets that can be applied to nearly everyone’s childhood.
When playing, the game makes your reminiscence not just about the time it is set in, but your own memories too. Therefore, Gone Home gives a complex and relatable feeling of nostalgia that has the potentially to appeal to many gamers, as opposed to just one age demographic.
The game also boasts some very interesting characters.
Katie’s father is a failed writer who is attempting to come to terms with the fact his book wasn’t a success.
Her mother is a wildlife conservationist who is trying to save her marriage.
And her sister, Sam, is making new friends through inviting people back to their allegedly haunted house.
Of course, there is much, much, MUCH more to these characters but I don’t want to spoil anything for anyone who is interesting in playing the game.
You learn so much about these characters, not only through Sam’s messages, but also through the little trinkets, letters and objects you can find throughout the house.
This is where the game truly shines. Through its mood and story-telling abilities, the game manages to make you care about characters you can’t even see.
Gone Home is a very short game and can easily be finished in an afternoon, even with thorough exploration.
However, there are lots of theories and lore online where players have speculated about the characters and the story. You can find several forums that discuss Gone Home in detail, which just proves how much the story impacts and envelopes you.
The story, where you dig deeper, can often be quite dark at times – the game realistically portraying the effects of many real-life tragedies and horrors.
As much as I personally love this game, the only thing I will say is that I don’t believe it is for everyone.
You can sometimes find yourself lost in the house with no real direction, unless you’ve paid completely attention to every little thing you’ve picked up.
For those who love exploring, this is no issue however I can recognise that players could get frustrated by this and could eventually give up on finding the story and thus the game ends as the whole point of Gone Home is its story and characters.
It is also possible to miss quite a lot and jump ahead of the story, if you managed to stumble upon a secret too early. But since this game is so short, it is very easy to go back and do things differently, to explore things in another order or to pay more attention to certain areas.
For those who enjoy touching stories, great characters and exploration games, I highly recommend Gone Home.

At first blush Outlast may seem like a bunch of jump scares, but it covers its horror bases pretty well. While fear of things that go bump in the night is certainly a driving factor in the game, there's plenty of true horror creepiness to be had here. Driven mainly by the game's excellent visual and auditory atmosphere, the mood is puncuated by Mount Massive's sometimes creepy, sometimes violent inhabitants, various cryptic missives that slowly reveal the story, and "notes" scribbled by the protagonist should the player use their camera to capture certain sights or events. The tried and true game mechanic of finding a way to keep your light on in the dark is bolstered by using the camera's night vision instead of a traditional light source. This ensures that there's always going to be dark spots and also that in order to see better you also have to partially obstruct your vision. It all lends itself to a horror risk vs reward system that often has you just as scared when the night vision is on. While the story is somewhat hackneyed, it's well enough told and compelling enough to drive the player with more than just "get me the hell out of here" as a goal. My one complaint would be the number of forced failures the game resorts to in order to drive the narrative. While they pay off in story, they're often a little frustrating. Overall, if you can stomach the gruesome visuals and brave the terror, Outlast is more than worth picking up.

A small gem.
Not really a game, more an interactive tale, "Gone Home" tells a sensitive, moving story about a difficult topic, with tact and occasional humor.
For those asking "why not a book or a movie, then?" I would respond: "pace".
The rhythm of each discovery is carefully set, each one at just the right "distance" - both spatially and chronologically - from the others - each one a treat - no matter if it's a masterfully delivered journal entry, or an old scrap of newspaper.
The slow walking speed of the character under the player's control is deliberate: a subliminal invitation to explore your near surrounding, to manipulate each object at hand. It feels a bit like the z-code games of old, for the nostalgic.
Both graphics and sound compartment are great, and still hold their own despite the game's age. The storytelling is, as already mentioned, good enough a reason alone to embark in this adventure.
It's been since "Oxenfree" that I haven't been so enthralled by a game, and while "Gone Home" is not for everyone, it sure will provide a long lasting memory to some.
PS: some people are complaining about the game's length. My experience is that exploring every single room, object, container, took about 4 hours (and left me wanting for more), so I guess it sort of depends if you are into the game or not.

For me, the best part about the Bioshock series wasn't the combat (though it was excellent in all three games and related DLC). It wasn't necessarily the setting (though Rapture remains a unique place in the annals of gamer history). It wasn't even, by and large, the philosophical content (though I have nothing but respect for the injection of heady concepts into what is typically a fairless brainless game genre). No, it was exploring the setting itself, looking at all the incidental details, picking up the audio logs and letting the whole gestalt tell me the story of the place. I've an inkling that this was the favorite part of the fine minds behind the Bioshock 2 DLC, Minerva's Den, which led directly to Gone Home.
You are Kaitlyn Greenbriar, a mid-1990s college student who has come to see her family at their new residence after a European tour. Problem is, when you get there, the house is utterly deserted and you have to look everything over to figure out what happened before you got there. There is something joyous about picking over every little detail of the place: plugging in garage band music on tape players, zooming in on small details of things you can't pick up, checking out pictures and reading over various bills, tickets, letters, articles and the like. By themselves, the details are nothing. Put together, they tell a profoundly moving story of an average American family of the period, complete with all the frustrations, moral compromises, weaknesses and missteps that come with it. Extra props to the designers on making the house so realistic on the incidental touches (even if the polygons don't always allow for a photo-realistic approach). Every room looks lived in, complete with bits of trash, empty pizza boxes and the occasional broken door or blown out light. There's even a fun little reference to Minerva's Den if you look close enough.
Make no mistake...if you hate walking simulators, having nothing to shoot or having puzzles no more challenging than finding a key or locker combination, you're going to hate this game. It will likely take you between 2 to 4 hours to get to the end and replay value is arguably limited. But in my mind, that's like saying a paperback novel you read again and again has limited entertainment value. The feeling I got at the end made it more than worth the $20 I paid for it. So if you'd like something a little different, check this one out.

I like where it went with some of the puzzles, but the way everything gels together it was quite a frustrating experience overall. I'd be hard-pressed to recommend it on, to be honest.

Banished is an amazingly built indie simulation game.  I say indie because it is built by Shining Rock Software which consists of one person.  He does everything from the art to the programming.  It is amazing what one person can accomplish.  Like it says on Banished’s own website the game is a throwback to the games that were played in the 90’s.  I am barely old enough to qualify to talk about those games, seeing as I was born in 1989, but even I can remember playing those early simulations games and loving them.  This game for me brings me back to those days when a Sim game of any sort could just waste away whole weeks of your time.  Whether it be Sim City or Sim Farm, those games were just the best.  And it wasn’t about the graphics or the immersion or anything that we usually talk about in games today, but it was about the fun factor.  The exploration and building of a little world that you created.
Banished is also a neat little game that you can’t win, but only survive.  And because of that I think most people will find the game boring because there isn’t really much that happens.  You plan and build a little settlement into a town.  Hours upon hours go by if you are doing it right as your town grows.  Eventually you just run out of resources and your little ecosystem comes crashing down all around you.  The game however is actually very hard because if you “overexpand” the same thing can happen and lives will be lost so it is important to plan ahead.
All in all I can wholeheartedly suggest that everyone should try Banished.  With my current disappointment in Sim City, Banished fills that gaming whole for me and then some.  It is a great game to pick up and play between gaming sessions and on those “raining” days where you just want to sit around and play a fun simple game.

I managed to put over 30 hours into this game in a barely 72 hour time spam. Very addictive and highly recommend it for someone who's looking for a great simulation game. Actually, it's more like a survival/simulation game imo.
But, you want everything in this game to be perfect. It can get pretty intense when your people start starving if you don't have enough food or a sickness breaks out and you don't have a herbalist and a physician.
One of the things I absolutely love about this game is that when you want to start over, it doesn't feel like a boring rut or anything like that. You just become so focused on getting crap right this time. The maps are also randomized as well.
One time, everything was going perfect for once. There was enough food, tools, clothing, firewood, etc. And the next thing I know, a tornado comes ripping through my village. Killed some villagers. Destroyed my town hall building, houses, fisheries. Mother nature is cold. And you will never ever be prepared for it.
Banished is also all about balance, such is life. You have to make sure your people are feed, happy, and healthy. As well as make sure you keep building enough houses for them to reproduce. The townsfolk also love their booze, it makes them happy. Do not have a village without a tavern for the love of god.
The villagers also have a mind of their own. At one point, my village was running low on food because I screwed up. And I go around clicking on houses, checking inventory. And this 16 year old woman was living all by herself and she was hoarding food. "On this episode of Hoarders...." She literally had over 200 servings of corn, 150 fish, 300 venison, etc. Are you freakin' kidding me? So you know what I did? Ordered to have her house tore down and then build a small cemetery out of the materials from her home. She became homeless. Thus she had no inventory. And died. Her grave being in that cemetery.
Overall, if you want a game that's addictive and repeatedly punishes you, get this.

The game has excellent sound design. As you perform an action in the game, whether it is changing the size of your fountain drink cup or throwing meat onto the hot grill, there is a pleasurable sound that follows. The game appears pretty simple, but actually has some depth. Each food has certain positives and negatives that you have to take into account when you plan your daily menu. A certain number of foods might be optimal in terms of profitability, and you may be tempted to include only those because you need cash, but I enjoy mastering as many foods as I own as possible. There are various other challenges, such as catering, which may require you to serve certain foods you might not be used to. Catering is a good idea, because you can make more money faster than you can in your restaurant.
Each type of food also carries certain chores with it, which you also must do to maintain your perfect combos. The health inspector shows up every once in awhile to make sure you are doing all your chores. There is equipment that allows you to expand the foods you can cook, mitigate negatives from food you're serving, and make your chores easier.  Lately I've been more into games like this, where the goals are clear, but you have some freedom in how you achieve those goals.
The main negative of this game is that it is repetitive and fairly demanding in terms of optimal gameplay. It's difficult to play over a long period of time, because you really need to pay attention to what you're doing. During a rush hour, you really have to keep track of which order has come in first & understand which tasks you should tackle first. You need to take cook times, length of chores, and customer patience into account. When I started having trouble with my health inspections, I first invested in an automatic dishwasher to mitigate my dish washing, which was my most time-consuming chore. After trash became the longest & most troublesome, I got the trash service. The game is very addictive, and because it can be demanding, ti is difficult to play for long periods of time. Sometimes you just have to put the pipe down and detox for awhile.

- The ai provide a good challenge, you can practice your new deck in gauntlet and it's not a complete free win like in magic duel.
- Look pretty.
- There's possible interaction during your opponent turn (not enough in my opinion but too much interaction really slow the pace of the game and keep a lot of players away, I can understand that).
- The game is REALLY generous with the free reward, a true f2p.
- There's a mobile app which work fine.
- The draft mode is fun, cheap and let you keep the card ! Also very generous in chest if you're good.
- Each color as a really different flavor from it's magic counterpart. Eternal has it's own identity, if you're a MTG player you can play both, they feel like different games. This not poor man magic.
- Also you'll see A LOT of complain about sigil screw / flood. I doesn't feel like a problem to me, if a game use a mana system you'll get too much / not enough mana sometime, you can't avoid it. The game feel unfair because of the mulligan system.
The cons :
- The mulligan system :
God I hate this mulligan system so much. If you decide not to keep your opening you get a second hand with between 2 and 5 sigil. And that's it, if your hand is unplayed well too bad, enjoy your free lose.
The paris mulligan is so much better. For those who don't know in a paris mulligan each player who chooses to mulligan shuffles his or her hand into their library and draws a new hand with one less card than before. You can repeat this process as much as you want. So the first time you mulligan draw only 6 cards, then 5, then 4 ...
Starting a game with 6 or 5 cards never feel good but at least you can still win. When your mulligan give you a 5 sigil 2 two drop what are you supposed to do ? Paris mulligan teach players what hand they can keep and what hand they must mulligan, the more you play the more intelligently you approach mulligan. When I lost because of mana flood / screw in MTG I often feel like it's my fault because I decided to keep a bad hand out of greed. Eternal mulligan is a total RNG fest that take away decision making from the players. The worst part is that the dev seems to be really proud of it so it's very unlikely to ever change.
- There's no casual mode yet, so trying new deck in pvp feel frustrating. This is really weird because I doubt it would be that hard to implement.
- The match are BO1 with no sideboard. This is really bad because you can't ajust your deck to your opponent. If you put an attachement removal in your deck and your opponent don't have any you have 4 dead cards. I hope in the future casual will be BO1 and ranked BO3 with a 15/20 cards sideboard.
- You must put at least 33% sigil in your deck. I don't like that, it feel too much if you want to play a really fast aggro deck. They put this limitation so people don't abuse their stupid mulligan system, so one more reason to hate it.
- I'm not a fan of the 75 cards format. They choose to put so much card to increase variance, but it doesn't work really well imo. If you ant variance just implement a singleton game mode. The limited card pool make it worse, you often feel forced to add card you don't really like. I not a huge problem though, unlike the mulligan system I can deal with it, I'm just not a fan.
In conclusion it's a great game with a lot of potential. If your a MTG player looking for a good digital alternative look no further. The mulligan system is terrible thought, too bad, it keep Eternal from being excellent.

So I never actually thought I'd like an online card game. I was always looking at it that that fun of playing a card game is intrinsically tied to talking to the person across the table from you, at least for me. If only so you can explain whatever insane and janky brew you put together.
But with the game being free, I decided to give this one a shot, and it's absolutely wonderful. This is the recommendation of someone who used to play Magic: The Gathering, but hasn't really had the time to pursue it since graduating highschool, and who really, truely loves building interesting decks: I love this game after only a few hours, and I have no reason to believe it's going to drop off. I'm super psyched to play more of this, this game is sweet. I'm happy I got into this instead of Hearthstone, let's put it that bluntly. If you're lookin' for a card game, dive into this one  for a bit and see if it's what you want. Worst case, you play around, spend nothing, and go elsewhere.

Let's see, where should I start with? The fact that I threw my mouse away in fright? The fact that I actually screamed in fright until the microphone made static sounds? The fact where my heart started beating faster than 200 miles an hour? This game, totally scares the heart out of you. It made me think that I was silly to think that Amnesia A Machine for Pigs was a scary game. All this time, I thought A Machine for Pigs was the scariest game of 2013, but then, this came out. I start to think I was living in a nutshell the first 5 minutes I played Outlast. I practically freaked out, threw my mouse away, and ran. But after that, I had to force myself to sit down and play. This game is really a life taker from the heart, and guaranteed to give you an epic experience of being chased. Dying will be at the bottom of your list in this game, but for now, I guess you gotta start thinking how you will play this, afraid, or like a boss? I couldn't explore all areas unfortunately, because of BATTERIES. But this fact makes the game more fun and frightening, especially seeing fatso with night vision (Fatso's a monster in the game). For non-horror gamers, I suggest you try out Amnesia A Machine for Pigs first. If you think that is scary and you're not gonna play it anymore, think twice before trying out Outlast. This game will make you squeal like a pig and eat away at your courage until the last thing you have in you is your sanity, then it goes for that too. The story is well organized, though I think for people who only want the story from horror games, people still are better off with Amnesia A Machine for Pigs. But if you want jumpscares and a horrifying game that will always haunt you when you walk in dark corridors, this is the true game for you. A must buy for hardcore horror fans. It is arguable though, if this is the scariest game. The jumpscares may not be so bad, but it has suspense that will keep your heart going at hundreds of miles an  hour with constant speed. Voice acting is well done too, the monsters are given a human but not quite human voice, and they will send chills up your spine. The environment is epic, it gave me this epic feeling that this monster was going to show up, and sadly, my instincts are mostly always right. Finding fatso in the dark isn't really what the average horror gamers want to do in their top 10 list of what to do in horror games. Anyway, diffrent torn up enemies will keep your adrenaline pumping, and their horrifying deaths will have you grasping more and more of the story. Monsters searching for you while you are hiding and suceeding will kill your horror spirit. The mechanics are awesome in this game too, they add new stuff that the average horror game doesn't have such as the ability to look back while running. Overall, I say this is truly a game worth buying, worth the $20. But remember my warning, this is NOT a game for the faint hearted... Anyway, if you are sort of a daredevil, get it now. You won't regret it.

This isnt a game.
This is a quick hour or two of story telling.  The medium may be a video game, but honestly it should not be considered as such.  It's subtle and doesnt try to be anything too grand, and at the end of the day it just makes me say, "Is that it?"
The only thing to talk about here is the story, as that is all there is.  It doesnt feel like great story.  Thats the short of it.  It is small, character driven (which is fine), but the inevitable question I kept coming back to is: So?  There is no point to this story.  The set up is fine but it never ammounts to anything.  This is the definition of bland.
I appreciate creators trying to explore new mediums and explore story telling, but this game comes to a horrible cross road of bland and over priced.
I would pay a dollar for this story.  It feels like something written in a creative arts class in college.  It's a solid A+ assignment no doubt, but that doesnt equate to being fit for publication to the masses.
More 'games' of this style in the future would be great, but this is not the one to launch the genre by any means.  It is worth the time it takes to play but not the price.  If you have it for free or incredibly cheap give it a go, but beyond that don't bother.

If you can grab Gone Home at $10 or less, it's a nice little game.  (I actually think a $5-$8 price is best).  I agree with everyone who complained about the $20 price point.  With it being 2 hours, it's just not worth that.  I can see some people wanting to play through a second time, but, if you take your time with the game, there really is no re-play value at all.  It's basically like reading short story which, in my opinion, is not worth $20.  Entire novels cost about that and I can't justify paying $20 for what would be like 1 chapter from a novel.
The visuals here are quite beautiful and the voice acting is good.  The controls are smooth and the atmosphere is great.  I enjoyed the way the game gives you little bits of information at a time, keeping you guessing.  It really does a great job of guiding you to discovering the life of this family. I think this is a great way to tell a story and would love to see more stories told like this.
However...
**spoiler alert**
What a disappointing ending.  With all the hints at something paranormal going on (references to ghost hunting, The X-Files, secret passages, etc.), I was really hoping for a darker ending that wasn't just a standard "happily ever after".  I think I would have felt more for Sam if her romance with Lennie had been tragic.  I would have felt more for the parents if they had split up instead of ending up at a retreat to fix their marriage.  Am I crazy for being disappointed with a happy ending?  It just felt so...disingenuous.  Everything up to the end made me believe something bad was going to happen.  I was actually shocked and disappointed when it ended up being all good.
**spoiler end**
Despite feeling that the ending was disingenuous, I liked this experience.  I think everyone should give this game a chance if the price is right.

The Crew is a good game despite the reviews and other stuff other people have said about it. It does have it's flaws, but they are far out-weighed by the Pros.
Pros:
-Vast Open World to explore (Bigger than Test Drive Unlimited/Test Drive Unlimited 2's map)

-Performance Parts for cars can be entirely earned without money by completing Skills in the Open World
Cons:
-Micro Transactions
-Payouts from missions and activities is low
-Car physics get buggy when driving over certain features (ie Rocks/Cliffs) [This can also be fun and make funny moments. so maybe not so much a bad thing]
-Campaign/Career is rather short.
-You must be connected to the internet at all times when you play
These are just a few of the pros and cons. Again the pros outweigh the cons, and cruising with your friends makes it even better. I would recommend getting the game on sale or at least getting the Season Pass to save money on the DLC. This game is overall a great game. I would give it a 8.5 out of 10. It has a lot of replay value, making it worth purchasing.

This game is probably gonna get me some hate from this review. First off let me say, I did enjoy the game, however I do have a few gripes that just got to me too much for me to justify me recommending this game.
First problem you might run into is how glitchy it is. Now I know open world games are glitchy, Trust me I've played a lot. This game however is the only one that has glitched on me on a regular basis. From being able to walk through solid objects, to being sling shotted all over the place for trying to grapple something. Chances are you will not experience one or two glitches but multiple glitches. Now these often times are easily fixed by dying but the next problem I have will show how bad this game can get.
Second, The size of the map. Many of you probably just got♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ but hear me out. The map is huge, I mean in a super sonic jet I still travel for a few minutes to locations in the same general area. I heard its like 400 square kilometers in size. Thats pretty massive, and a good thing for some open world games, but not this one. The main problem is the respawner, it will put you back at the closet stronghold, this means you can travel from one end of the map to the other, die and end up back where you left. The long travel times will slowly wear you away till you are just ready to stop playing because of how long it takes. There is a fast travel system but if you dont have a location nearby (you have to pick a village, base, or stronghold) you will still have to travel a long time.
Third, Some people have said the game feels full and alive, I disagree, this map feels empty and lifeless. The people act like idiots barely able to function, they will turn and run when guns are shot, but thats about it. They walk around a little bit, but they never do anything that makes me think they are alive. Even your allies seem to take a few seconds to register that an enemy even exists. There is no wildlife, You are in a huge jungle map with no reason to go into the jungle, a game like Far Cry 3 has a similer setting and i have a reason to go into the wild, I can hunt and kill. If you removed all the jungle areas you would have a much easier to travel area and would miss nothing because nothing is there.
Fourth, The characters. This one is more of an irk, If my character is hispanic, Why oh god why does the Asian accented population just not care?! I mean at one point I used a radio to try and get a prisoner out into the yard so I could save him. Guess what, no one questioned why there was a spanish guy outside. If no one is allowed onto the island why the ♥♥♥♥ does no one care when I speak?
Those are my gripes, The game looks fantastic graphically  in the open world but when it gets close to the models in cutscenes you really notice how bad they are up close. The controls are fine, but can get annoying when you try to grapple up a building. Chaos is kinda pointless since thats all you can do, least in a game like GTA I can pretend to be a normal human and thus makes it fun to cause chaos. With the lifelessness of the NPCs you dont get any satisfaction out of killing them. Overall I wouldnt play it if i had another game to play. Many other open world games out there Far Cry 3 and GTA 4 (soon 5 for pcs) just did it better. Also no one get on my case about the multiplayer, I would add that into this review if it wasnt a mod! I dont care if its supported by steam, If it was added to the game I would include it here, the game must hold up on its own.

There are some reasons to dislike 'The Crew' but one that makes the game a recommendation – it's fun.
Pros:
- Enormous map of the U.S.A.
- Very interesting, long campaign, almost like a movie. IMO best story ever in a racing game. 65 Missions
- Some extremely long races. 2.5 hours from Miami to Los Angeles via New York!!!
(Perfect to turn your head off after a long day at the office)
- Nice graphics (if you find the right settings)
- Many ways to improve your cars.
- Cars can be tuned into street, off-road, performance, race or rally cars.
(some cars can only be tuned into some of the types)
- Visual tuning
- Performance tuning
- Co-op missions
- Cockpit view
- Different radio stations
- Country side looks fantastic (cities not always)
- Total open world, also in all races
- All cars feel different
- Police (but too easy to escape)
- Tons of mini games
- All kind of animals, the crocodiles in the New Orleans swamps look fantastic
- day/night cycle
- addictive
Cons:
- Frame-rate sometimes drops, especially in cities. Changing graphic settings does not prevent this.
- Car handling isn't the best in the beginning of the game but gets better after improving individual car settings
- Very hard to make money, but you need money to buy cars. After 40 hours of playing I only have like 10 cars. There are about 50 cars in the game but you have to consider the different race-types (race, rally, etc.) So you can have like 200 different cars if you have the money. (not all cars support all types)
- You can buy game money with real money :-(((
- Some cars can only be bought with real money :-(((
...but you do not need them to win in MP
- Permanent on-line connection required
- Game takes long to start
- Upgrading cars is time consuming and can be frustrating. Every car can be upgraded to max level 1299. You need to play tests (hill climb, slalom, speed test, escape, etc.) to collect upgrade kits. But the game randomly decides which upgrade level you will receive. So even if you successfully complete the test you might not get the upgrade part you need. If you attempt to upgrade a car that already has a high level you can repeat tests like 50 times without being granted with the missing part, although you succeeded the test 50 times. Alternatively you can buy missing car parts but only if you have already earned the desired upgrade level and the fact that the game keeps you low on money makes upgrading by buying parts a painful decision.
- MP race selection can be frustrating. Before each mp event every player can select their favorite event. Players can select the track, the car type and mp event type (racing, king of the crown, etc.). They can decide to activate or deactivate contact with other players and activate or deactivate traffic. A random selection carried out by the game will decide who's player selection will be played next.
- High influence of luck in MP if you play with crash kids. You can lead 90% of a race but if someone pushes you into a field at 300 kph you're almost certain to become last. IMO it's best to select races with deactivated player contact but it's a matter of luck if you will play such race or not because the game decides which event is going to be played.
- AI is too easy most of the time
- Not a MMO. Eight simultaneous players in free drive mode
- No rain, no snow, no weather conditions
- Uplay
- If Ubisoft servers are unavailable you can not play.
- Sometimes mp players seem to cheat, but very rarely.
'The Crew' is not a serious racing game like 'Dirt', 'Grid' or 'Project Cars'. It's an arcade fun racer in a cozy, feel good world that simply looks fantastic. The star of the game is the enormous and beautiful U.S.A. and the story.
